//: Global pyright fallback. Pyright walks UP from the file being checked and uses the nearest pyrightconfig.json, so a copy at $HOME governs any project that does not carry its own -- verified: a config in a parent directory silenced a diagnostic in a child. A project's own pyrightconfig.json or [tool.pyright] wins, which is the intended override path.
//why-not-lsp: These belong in a file rather than in lsp.json's `settings`, because OMP does not answer the server's `workspace/configuration` request -- a settings block there is inert today. Filed separately; this mechanism works now.
//mode: standard is pyright's own default and is kept deliberately. strict would fail on every unannotated third-party call in projects that never opted in, and a gate that fires everywhere is one people learn to ignore.
//imports: A config at $HOME cannot know where any given project's virtualenv lives, so unresolved imports would be noise on every file. Same ruling rqgm makes, for the same reason: the type checker reports type errors, and the import resolver is not one.
//escalation: Rules that catch a bug reaching runtime rather than a style preference.
//advisory: Real signal, kept at warning because a global default that errors on these would fail existing code never written against them.
//off: Ruff already owns these and says it better. Two tools reporting one defect trains people to read neither.
